extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of mathematics/physics; readers of Archimedes' On Floating Bodies (advanced undergraduate/graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting the propositions and stability criteria given by Archimedes (Book I & II) about floating and submerged solids, their equilibrium positions, and the forces involved (buoyancy, apparent weight, stability conditions for spherical and paraboloid segments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluid surface concentric spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections of the surface by planes through O (centre of the earth) are circumferences of circles whose centre is O; therefore the surface is that of a sphere with centre O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: unequal pressures would set fluid in motion; equality of pressures on symmetric sections forces spherical symmetry. Used as background geometric fact in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral buoyancy for equal-weight solids (Prop. 3, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of solids those which, size for size, are of equal weight with a fluid will, if let down into the fluid, be immersed so that they do not project above the surface but do not sink lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs pyramids with vertex at O and compares pressures on corresponding parts of fluid; unequal pressures would cause motion, contradiction. Emphasises equality of pressure on symmetric fluid parts as equilibrium condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lighter solids cannot be completely submerged (Prop. 4, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: A solid lighter than a fluid will, if immersed in it, not be completely submerged, but part of it will project above the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction using pyramids and spheres centered at O; unequal pressures on fluid parts if solid were completely submerged would produce motion, violating rest hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibrium immersion equals displaced-fluid weight (Archimedes' principle) (Prop. 5, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any solid lighter than a fluid will, if placed in the fluid, be so far immersed that the weight of the solid will be equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses same pyramid/sphere construction and equality of pressures at corresponding fluid parts to deduce weight equality between solid and displaced fluid (the fundamental statement of buoyancy at equilibrium).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upthrust equals difference of weights when forcibly immersed (Prop. 6, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a solid lighter than a fluid be forcibly immersed in it, the solid will be driven upwards by a force equal to the difference between its weight and the weight of the fluid displaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructs an auxiliary solid so combined weight is less than equal volume of fluid and uses equilibrium of the combined body to deduce that the upward force on the originally immersed solid equals the weight difference (i.e., buoyant force = displaced fluid weight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy solids sink and apparent weight reduction (Prop. 7, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: A solid heavier than a fluid will, if placed in it, descend to the bottom; when weighed in the fluid the solid will be lighter than its true weight by the weight of the fluid displaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First part: mechanical reasoning about pressure under the solid causes it to descend. Second part: combine with a light auxiliary solid to form a neutrally buoyant combination and deduce that the apparent loss of weight equals the weight of displaced fluid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postulate: direction of upward forcing (Postulate 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies which are forced upwards in a fluid are forced upwards along the perpendicular [to the surface] which passes through their centre of gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly to locate the line of action of buoyant forces in stability arguments (i.e., the buoyant force acts along a vertical through the centre of gravity of the displaced fluid portion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spherical-segment stable orientation: axis perpendicular (Prop. 8, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a solid in the form of a segment of a sphere, and of a substance lighter than a fluid, be immersed in it so that its base does not touch the surface, the solid will rest in such a position that its axis is perpendicular to the surface; if forced into a position touching on one side and released, it returns to the symmetrical (axis-perpendicular) position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof (partly missing in Latin version) compares centres of gravity of immersed and emerged parts and uses lines of action through O to show torques drive the segment back to the perpendicular axis position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spherical-segment with base below surface: axis perpendicular (Prop. 9, Book I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a solid in the form of a segment of a sphere, and of a substance lighter than a fluid, be immersed in it so that its base is completely below the surface, the solid will rest in such a position that its axis is perpendicular to the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutilated proof in surviving version; treats cases depending on whether segment is greater than, equal to, or less than a hemisphere; reasoning uses centres of gravity and relative torques to reach perpendicular axis equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight-to-fluid-weight ratio equals immersed-volume-to-whole ratio (Book II Prop. 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a solid lighter than a fluid be at rest in it, the weight of the solid will be to that of the same volume of the fluid as the immersed portion of the solid is to the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algebraic statement equivalent to Archimedes' principle: weight(solid) : weight(same volume of fluid) = immersed_volume : total_volume; derived by comparing weights of equal volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability for paraboloid segments: short axis (Book II Prop. 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a right segment of a paraboloid of revolution whose axis is not greater than 3p (p = parameter), and whose specific gravity is less than that of a fluid, be placed in the fluid with its axis inclined to the vertical at any angle but with base not touching the surface, the segment will not remain in that position but will return to the position in which its axis is vertical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a cross-section parabola, tangent parallel to surface chord, centers of gravity of submerged and emerged parts, and geometric inequalities (AN ≤ 3p) to show torques restore vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability for paraboloid segments: short axis, base submerged (Book II Prop. 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a right segment of a paraboloid of revolution whose axis is not greater than 3p and whose specific gravity is less than that of a fluid be placed in the fluid with its axis inclined and its base entirely submerged, the solid will not remain in that position but will return to the vertical axis position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous geometric argument to Prop. 2 applied to the case where base is completely submerged, again comparing centers of gravity and lines of action to show restoring torque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability for paraboloid segments: axis > 3p with specific gravity threshold (Book II Prop. 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right segment of a paraboloid of revolution whose axis AN is greater than 3p, and whose specific gravity is less than that of the fluid but bears to it a ratio not less than (AN — 3p)² : AN², if the segment be placed with axis inclined and base not touching surface, it will not remain but will return to vertical axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise numeric condition on specific gravity relative to geometry (involving AN and p). Proof computes centres and shows CL perpendicular to tangent, producing restoring torque when ratio condition holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary stability condition for submerged base (Book II Prop. 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right segment with axis AM > 3p and specific gravity less than fluid but in a ratio to it not greater than {AM² — (AM — 3p)²} : AM², if placed with axis inclined but base completely submerged, it will return to vertical axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the complementary inequality (upper bound on specific gravity ratio) for stability when base is entirely submerged; proof similar to Prop. 4 with algebraic inequalities relating immersed portion to whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instability when base touches surface at one point (Book II Prop. 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a right segment of a paraboloid lighter than a fluid has axis AM > 3p but AM:4p < 15:4 and is placed with its axis so inclined that its base touches the fluid, it will never remain with its base touching the surface in one point only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction introduces special measures (CK chosen so AM:CK = 15:4), tangents, diameters and center-of-gravity arguments to show that torques force rotation rather than equilibrium when touching at a single point.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single-point base contact equilibrium for certain submerged conditions (Book II Prop. 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the same dimensional/specific-gravity constraints as Prop. 6 (AM > 3p but AM:4p < 15:4), if the base is entirely submerged the segment will never rest with the base touching the surface at only one point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses analogous geometric construction and centre-of-gravity lines to Prop. 6 to deduce inability to have equilibrium with single-point base contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of oblique equilibrium (Book II Prop. 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right segment of a paraboloid with axis AM > 3p and AM:4p < 15:4 whose specific gravity bears to that of the fluid a ratio less than (AM — 3p)² : AM², then if placed with its axis inclined and base not touching the fluid, the solid will not return to the vertical and will have equilibrium only in a certain oblique position (axis at a specific angle to the surface).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides conditions under which the vertical position is not restoring and a unique oblique stable equilibrium occurs; proof divides into cases depending on angle and uses center-of-gravity alignment to find the equilibrium angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary oblique equilibrium condition (Book II Prop. 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right paraboloid segment with axis AM > 3p and AM:4p < 15:4 whose specific gravity bears to that of the fluid a ratio greater than {AM² — (AM — 3p)²} : AM², then when placed with axis inclined and base entirely below surface it will not return to vertical but will rest in a certain oblique position determined as in Prop. 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirror-image criterion to Prop. 8: when specific gravity is larger than a threshold, the equilibrium oblique angle exists and is characterized by center-of-gravity collinearity; proof again uses geometric constructions with tangents and diameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of positions of rest for long-axis paraboloid segments (Book II Prop. 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a right segment of a paraboloid with axis AM such that AM:4p > 15:4, for a segment placed in a fluid of greater specific gravity with its base entirely above the surface, the positions of rest are determined by a detailed geometric construction involving similar parabolic segments, tangents, diameters, and centers of gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition lays out a systematic geometric method (divide axis, draw auxiliary parabolas, locate tangents, diameters and centres) to investigate possible equilibria and their stability for the case of a long axis and base above surface; used as algorithmic procedure rather than a single inequality.
